---
title: "Set Up and First Render"
subtitle: "Install two programs, open the project, and see a finished website within the hour"
---

::: {.objectives}
**In this chapter**

- Explain in one sentence how text files become a course website
- Install R and RStudio
- Open the project and build the website for the first time
- Make one change and see it appear
:::

## The idea in three sentences

You write your course as ordinary text files, one per chapter. You press one
button, and the software turns those files into a finished website: navigation,
search, quizzes, the university's colours and logo, all included. That website
is just a folder of files, which you then put on GitHub or GitLab, where it is
shown to learners as a normal web address.

Think of it like exporting a Word document to PDF. You write, you press export,
you get the finished thing. The difference is that the "finished thing" is a
whole website, and that this one already looks the way the university expects.

::: {.keypoint}
**Key point**

You never edit the website itself. You edit the text files and *render* (build)
the website again. If something on the website is wrong, you fix the text file,
not the web page.
:::

## Step 1: install R and RStudio

Two free programs, installed in this order.

1. **R** — the engine underneath. Download from
   [cran.r-project.org](https://cran.r-project.org): choose your operating
   system, then the download link for the latest version, and run the
   installer with the default choices.
2. **RStudio Desktop** — the program you actually work in. Download from
   [posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/)
   and install it.

RStudio includes **Quarto**, the tool that builds the website. There is nothing
else to install.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## You will not write R code

This template contains no R code, and you do not need to know any. R is only the
engine that RStudio runs on. You will work with text, images and quiz questions.
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## On a managed work computer

If you are not allowed to install programs, ask your IT support for R and
RStudio Desktop. Many institutions offer them through a software portal. Tell
them you need *RStudio Desktop with Quarto*, so they install a version recent
enough to include it.
:::

## Step 2: put the project in the right place

You receive the template as a folder (or a zip file, which you unzip first).

1. Copy the folder to a normal location on your own computer, such as
   *Documents*.
2. Rename it to something that describes your course, for example
   `wound-care-course`. Use lowercase letters and hyphens; avoid spaces,
   umlauts and special characters.
3. Inside, rename `course-template.Rproj` to the same name, for example
   `wound-care-course.Rproj`.

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
## Avoid synchronised and network folders

Keep the project on the computer's own disk. Folders that are continuously
synchronised (cloud storage) or that live on a network drive can be slow and can
lock files while the website is being built, which causes confusing errors.
:::

## Step 3: open the project and build the website

1. Double-click the `.Rproj` file. RStudio opens with the project loaded.
2. Find the **Build** tab, usually in the upper-right panel.
3. Click **Render Website**.

The first build takes a minute or two. Progress appears in a panel labelled
*Background Jobs*, and when it finishes, the website opens in RStudio's Viewer
pane or in your browser. That is your course, running.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## If there is no Build tab

RStudio only shows it when the project was opened through the `.Rproj` file.
Use *File → Open Project…* and choose that file.
:::

The finished website is written to a folder called `docs` inside your project.
Chapter 8 explains why it has that name and what to do with it. For now, just
know that this folder is the product: everything a learner sees is in there.

## Step 4: your first edit

1. In RStudio's *Files* panel, click `index.qmd` to open it.
2. Change the `title:` line at the top to something of your own.
3. Save (*Ctrl+S*, or *Cmd+S* on a Mac).
4. Click **Render Website** again.

Your new title appears. That is the whole working rhythm of this course:
**edit, save, render, look.** Repeat as often as you like; nothing you do can
break the original, and a render is harmless.

### Editing without seeing the markup

The file you just opened shows some symbols (`#`, `*`, `:::`). That is the
*source* view. You do not have to live there. At the top-left of the editor
there are two buttons, **Source** and **Visual**. Click **Visual** and the file
looks like a word processor: bold and italic buttons, bullet lists, an *Insert*
menu for pictures, tables and callouts. The text underneath is written for you.

Most authors work in Visual mode and switch to Source only to fix something
particular. Chapters 3 and 4 show both views side by side.

## What if something goes wrong?

| What you see | What it usually means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| An error message in the Background Jobs panel | A typo in a text file. The message names the file and often the line | Open that file, look at the line named, compare with a working example |
| The error mentions the settings file, `_quarto.yml` | Wrong indentation. That file is fussy about spaces | Use spaces, never the Tab key; copy an existing block and change only the words |
| The page still shows old content | It was not rebuilt | Click **Render Website** again and refresh the browser (*Ctrl+F5*) |
| Search does not work when you double-click a page in `docs` | Search needs the site to be *served*, not opened from disk | Use the preview RStudio gives you after rendering, or check search once the site is published |
: Common first-day problems {#tbl-troubleshooting}

## Check your understanding

::: {.quiz-score}
:::

::: {.question}
You spot a spelling mistake on a page of the finished website. Where do you fix it?

- [ ] In the HTML file inside the `docs` folder
- [x] In the `.qmd` text file, then render the website again
- [ ] In the browser, by clicking on the text
- [ ] In the `.Rproj` file

::: {.feedback}
The website is generated from the text files. If you correct the generated file,
your fix is overwritten the next time you render. Always correct the source.
:::
:::

::: {.question}
Do you need to know how to program in R to use this template?

- [ ] Yes, at least the basics
- [x] No. R is only the engine RStudio runs on; you work with text and menus
- [ ] Yes, but only to build the quizzes
- [ ] Only if the course has images

::: {.feedback}
The template contains no R code. Quizzes are written as plain text, and images
and tables are inserted from menus or with a few characters of markup.
:::
:::

The working rhythm of this course is: edit, save, [?]{.fitb answer="render"}, look.
(Type the missing word and click elsewhere. *Render* is the word for building the
website from the text files; in RStudio it is the **Render Website** button.)
